WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (retail_payment_servicing, env_0066). Status: round 1 closed; REWORK round 2 applied (see section 11).

0. DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 4]}. Assignment: retail_ext_good_faith_payment = 6 factors; retail_ext_returned_installment_late_charge = 4; retail_ext_arrears_payment = 4; retail_ext_extension_grant = 4.

1. WHY A GOOD TEST. The customer (Tamara Ellison, Tier 4 retail contract 1062847315) asks only that the extension she e-signed be put through. A real Kestrel servicing agent must discover from the extension rule that (a) the August installment re-opened by her returned mailed check owes a late charge that has to stand before the installment is deferred (no late charge can be assessed on a deferred installment), (b) an agent-taken arrears payment toward the other past-due installment (2026-09-20) must post, and (c) she must make a good-faith payment herself on the automated line, and that the extension fee itself depends on the money posted. Every amount comes from reading the charter, the posting history, the lease ledger and the tier, never from choosing among similar tools: each write has exactly one policy and one tool.

2. SCOPE / BUDGET. Task 0 claims retail_ext_returned_installment_late_charge, retail_ext_arrears_payment, retail_ext_good_faith_payment, retail_ext_extension_grant and tools assess_returned_installment_late_charge_34170c70, post_arrears_payment_6321a7ae, submit_extension_good_faith_payment_c7575c9b (owner=user), grant_retail_extension_6a93006b. Task 1 (draw 2 prerequisites, [4,6,6]) keeps the disjoint catch-up tree: retail_ext_catch_up_payment (owner=user), retail_ext_unpaid_installment_late_charge, retail_ext_late_posted_installment_late_charge. The claim's other events (waiver, due-date change, restriction update) carry no amount a tier ladder can compute (a waiver is always of the whole fee; a due-date change carries only day numbers and dates) — recorded in plan, so the seven computational writes are the three late-charge situations, the extension fee and three distinct payments.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: retail_ext_extension_grant (on_request, computes extension_fee). Edges:
 E1 extension_grant -> returned_installment_late_charge, kind state_gate, gate retail_transactions.installment_due_date, form state, sentence "The extension is not granted until the installment it defers, when a returned payment re-opened it and its grace period has ended, shows its late charge in the contract's ledger." Seed: retail_transactions ret_2026-08 (2026-09-01, reverses the 2026-08-18 payment for installment 2026-08-20); no retail_late_charge with installment_due_date 2026-08-20. Only the re-opened-installment late charge tool books that state. Deletion: terminal ledger lacks the 4.00 charge (extension_fee unchanged at 4.00).
 E2 extension_grant -> arrears_payment, value_input, gate method_fee, form state, sentence "The extension is granted only after a payment through the agent-assisted phone ACH channel has posted on the contract since its most recent installment due date." Seed: last_payment_date 2026-08-18 and that payment returned; no phone_agent_ach payment exists. Only post_arrears_payment writes phone_agent_ach. Deletion: extension_fee 4.00 -> 13.00.
 E3 extension_grant -> good_faith_payment, value_input, gate method_fee, form action ("The extension fee is fixed only after the customer has made the good-faith payment toward the extension, wherever the good-faith amount for the extension is above 0.00."), fallback: the good-faith payment leaves a phone_ivr_ach payment indistinguishable from the catch-up payment of task 1. Deletion: 4.00 -> 13.00.
 E4 good_faith_payment -> returned_installment_late_charge, value_input, gate risk_pct, state ("The good-faith amount is figured only after the installment the contract's next due date shows, when a returned payment has re-opened it and its grace period has ended, carries its late charge on the contract."). Deletion: 467.41 -> 370.51.
 E5 arrears_payment -> returned_installment_late_charge, value_input, gate fee_carry, state ("The arrears payment amount is worked out only once the late charge owed on the installment the contract's next due date shows, when a returned payment has re-opened it, stands on the contract."). Deletion: 545.83 -> 444.93.
 Topological order: late charge (step 10) -> arrears payment (12) -> good-faith payment (14, customer's own) -> extension (16). Arrears and good-faith commute (neither reads the other's write; the extension reads only their sum). value_input edges: 4 >= max(3-1,1)=2. Directions: "not ... until" (negated) and "only after/only once" (affirmative) both used. user_scenario names none of these problems.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. retail_late_charges: late_status (status active), grace_elapsed (anchor next_due_date 2026-08-20; first permissible 2026-08-31; boundary exclusive; frozen 2026-09-28 past it), one_per_installment (no late charge for 2026-08-20; the only late charge row is for 2025-04-20). retail_payment_posting payable_status (active) for both payments; retail_reinstatement_and_redemption has no gate on installment payments (policy_scope). retail_extensions: x_status active; x_counts payments_made_count 20 >= 9, days_past_due 39 <= 45, extensions 0 + 1 <= 3; x_blackout remaining 60 + 0 - 20 = 40 > 6; x_relationship: pre-owned closed, balloon closed, lease active (not repossessed/charged off); x_signed: request extension_agreement completed 2026-09-24 (sent 2026-09-22, within 10 days); x_interval: never extended, no interval. Overwrites: good-faith clause of retail_extensions (scoped to good-faith payments, keeps the posting window and the none-required case); extension-fee clause (scoped to extensions under this policy); late-charge formula clause of retail_late_charges (scoped to re-opened installments; tail names the unpaid and late-posted cases handled by their own schedules).

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: contract R (account 1062847315), installment 2026-08-20 (re-opened by the reversal of payment pay_2026-08-20, 646.04, returned 2026-09-01 insufficient_funds, fee 25.00 booked). Other past-due installment 2026-09-20 (grace through 2026-09-30, no late charge owed yet). Excluded rows: 2025-05-01 late charge (2025-04-20 installment, outside every 12-month window; paid by the 2025-05-18 fee portion), lease late charge 2025-06-07 (outside 12 months), closed pre-owned (paid 2024-11-08 at trade-in) and closed balloon (paid 2023-06-12).

6. FACTOR CARD (sensitivity from the Step 5 run; baseline = standard method).
 Late charge 4.00 (all-baseline 25.00): lrf_tenure_rate 3.0% (20 satisfied, 0 late in 12m) base->11.00; lrf_first_return_relief halve+floor (only return ever, never extended) base->14.38; lrf_lessee_deduction 3.00 (lease: 12 payments, 0 late; cross-difficulty) base->7.00; lrf_lapsed_grace 2.00 (return lag 12 > 10) base->6.00.
 Arrears 545.83 (all-baseline 646.04): cuf_arrears_share 85% base->642.74; cuf_lessee_share -10 pts base->610.44; cuf_exposure +5 pts (37 months to maturity, Tier 4) base->513.53; cuf_fee_carry whole fees 29.00 base->516.83.
 Good faith 467.41 (all-baseline 323.02): gff_delinquency_risk 75% (multi-source: returned AND late) base->305.90; gff_lessee_points 10 (cross-difficulty) base->532.02; gff_tenure_points 5 (21 months on books) base->499.72; gff_first_hardship 5 (no extension/due-date entry) base->499.72; gff_long_term +7 (Tier 4, contract length 60 months) base->422.19; gff_overdue_interest 9 days x 7.43 base->400.54.
 Extension fee 4.00 (all-baseline 35.00): xf_fee_method halved (recent payments 1013.24 >= 646.04) base->22.00; xf_history_reduction 5 base->9.00; xf_lessee_reduction 5 base->9.00; xf_first_extension 3 base->7.00.
 Near-misses: 2025-05-01 late charge (counts only with a window > 12 months); lease late charge 2025-06-07; the returned Aug payment (txn_date 2026-08-18) is not a recent payment for the fee method (posted before 2026-08-29); maturity months 37 vs threshold 36.

7. PERSONA. Tired, plain-spoken office manager; volunteers only the signed extension request; identity on request (phone 3135512746, DOB 1987-06-14, ZIP 28203, email, SSN last4 1752, account 1062847315); authorizes an agent-taken payment from checking 1438 only after the agent explains one is needed; runs the automated-line payment herself for the amount the agent gives; accepts charges without arguing; ends when told the extension is granted. No hint of late charge, return, arrears or good faith.

8. STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB, ZIP) -> read retail contract, ledger, requests, lease, lease ledger, pre-owned, balloon -> assess re-opened late charge 4.00 on 2026-08-20 -> arrears payment 545.83 (1438) -> customer's good-faith payment 467.41 (1438) -> grant extension (request Q, installment 2026-08-20, 1 installment, good_faith_amount 467.41, fee 4.00).

9. VERIFICATION (b/run_t0.py via check_compute machinery): LR 4.0 base 25.0; CU 545.83 base 646.04; GF 467.41 base 323.02; X 4.0 base 35.0; skip LR -> X 4.0, skip CU -> X 13.0, skip GF -> X 13.0, skip LR -> GF 370.51, skip LR -> CU 444.93. Gates --task 0: EXTENDED OK / TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK / REPLAY OK / SOLVABILITY OK / COMPUTE OK / GROUNDING OK / SCOPE OK.

10. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Reading only the published rules (hub + factor sentences), the tool schemas and the finder returns, the agent can see: the August installment is next due and its payment was returned after grace -> re-opened late charge; the September installment is past due -> arrears payment; good faith is required -> customer's automated-line payment; then the extension. Each figure above follows from the rule sentences with the records listed; no second reading was found (order of combination is stated in each rule's assembly sentence).

REVISIONS. (r1) check_extended: every factor must rest on at least one record read; the factors that read only plain fields were given record reads (GFP tenure: MONTHS from first payment; GFP/EXT first-hardship/first-extension: COUNT of extension and due-date entries; GFP interest: DAYS from next due date; ARR exposure: MONTHS to maturity). Factors that also read a counter field alongside a record count (RLC/ARR/EXT payments_made_count, RLC extensions_used_lifetime) keep that field next to their ledger counts. (r2) replay closure: added pre-owned/balloon finders (relationship gate evidence). (r3) method transforms moved to mode selectors so no factor reads another factor (sweep: factor-cross [] for all policies). (r4) first-match reads removed (Care plan by EXISTS with the account filter; lease pull by XCOUNT).


11. REWORK round 2 (audit audits/policy_task/retail_payment_servicing, round 1).
 - CG-2: the three prerequisite sentences on the re-opened late charge (extension, good faith, arrears) now name the installment the contract's next due date shows (for the extension: the installment it defers), matching both their conditions and the reach of the re-opened late-charge policy; conditions copied into prerequisite_closure verbatim.
 - O-2: the extension's arrears sentence names the record-visible channel ("a payment through the agent-assisted phone ACH channel") instead of a performer. O-3: edge effect texts state what the write changes in general terms, not one world's tier move.
 - O-1: the arrears and good-faith policies (and the catch-up policy) declare an overwrite of the base allocation sentence: the payment is recorded on its posting day and the nightly posting cycle applies it in payment_allocation_order; the three replaced_by texts name each other's cases; the payment tool docstrings say the split is applied by the nightly cycle, not by the call; the arrears fee carry now says the amount includes an amount equal to the fees.
 - O-5: the early-life points (months since contract date, which cancelled the tenure points) are replaced by long-term exposure points on a different dimension (contract length, contract date to maturity, >= 60 months on Tier 4/5 -> 7 points, other tiers 2.5); good-faith amount recomputed (section 6 and 9 figures updated).
 - O-9: the arrears amount subtracts one monthly payment for each installment the most recent completed signed extension agreement defers (read from the agreement), not always one.
 - O-13 (CG-1 class): the re-opened late-charge rule states that a re-opened installment is not one paid in full within the grace period and compares the minimum unpaid portion with the re-opened amount.
 - Seeds: lease holding rebuilt to the lease charter (36 payments including signing: 30 made + 6 remaining, signing payment and funding rows on the ledger, depreciation 274.36 so the balance runs to the residual; adjusted lease balance = funding less depreciation); interest_paid_to_date set to the last posting date; pre-owned and balloon rows added to seed_consistency.
 - Minor: prerequisite_closure step numbers (10/12/14), order_uniqueness read lists, REVISIONS (r1) wording, persona timing ("Last week" for an agreement sent 2026-09-22 and signed 2026-09-24, before Monday 2026-09-28).
 - Re-run: LR 4.00 (base 25.00), arrears 545.83 (base 646.04), good faith 467.41 (base 323.02; sensitivities 305.90 / 532.02 / 499.72 / 499.72 / 422.19 / 400.54), extension fee 4.00 (base 35.00); skip late charge -> good faith 370.51, arrears 444.93; skip arrears or good faith -> fee 13.00; both payment orders identical.

12. REWORK round 3 (audit revision_2: charter CG-3; leftovers; XF recipe).
 - CG-3: the re-opened late-charge policy no longer takes the dishonoured payment's whole amount; its re-opened amount is the unpaid portion, as of the assessment date, of the installment the next due date shows (past_due_amount less one monthly_payment for each whole monthly_payment in the past_due_amount less one cent), the same measure the unpaid-installment policy now states, and its own rule states the minimum-unpaid and deferred-installment exclusions on that amount. The late-posted policy's overwrite tail (unpaid portion as of the assessment date for re-opened and unpaid installments) now reads identically against both. On this world the measure gives 1292.08 - 646.04 = 646.04, as before.
 - Leftover: the arrears factor trace now names step 10 for the late charge.
 - XF recipe applied to all seven policies (assembly sentences generic, counting conventions stated, ties, scope branches, tails, tool docstrings without 'toward'); figures unchanged (re-run: 4.00 / 545.83 / 467.41 / 4.00, sensitivities and baselines unchanged).

13. REWORK round 4 (audit revision_3: charter CG-4, CG-5).
 - CG-4: the arrears policy's standard method now defines the arrears share (standard_share_pct, 100 percent, applied to the other past-due amount); the share schedule replaces it, the lessee and exposure points add to or deduct from it, and the single combination sentence fixes the order generically (replacement first, then additions and deductions, one share applied once and rounded). Figures unchanged: 545.83 (base 646.04).
 - CG-5: the arrears and good-faith policies' allocation overwrites now restate the base allocation order for every other payment instead of deferring to the base rule; the re-opened late-charge overwrite restates the base late-charge figure for every other late charge.

14. REWORK round 5 (KB audit source items).
 - SRC-1: the three payment tools now post on the posting day the base posting rule gives: today when the payment is received earlier than 8:00 p.m. Central Time on a business day, otherwise the next business day (weekends and US federal holidays, a weekend holiday observed on the nearest weekday, are skipped); the last payment date becomes that day and the docstrings say so. The frozen time here (Monday 2026-09-28, 10:20 EDT) posts both payments today, so no figure moves.
 - SRC-2: the good-faith overwrite again keeps the clause's ordering ("before the extension is granted, a good-faith payment of at least that amount must still have posted since the most recent installment due date"), and the extension's action-form sentence now reads "... wherever the good-faith amount for the extension is above 0.00", so a 0.00 good-faith amount neither requires a payment nor holds the fee; condition updated to match. Here the good-faith amount is 467.41, so the edge applies as before.
user_scenario:
You are Tamara Ellison, a 39-year-old dental office manager in Charlotte, North Carolina. You finance a 2025 Kestrel Talon SE AWD with Kestrel Financial Services, and a pay cut at work has left you behind. Last week a Kestrel representative emailed you an extension agreement and you signed it electronically. You are calling because you want that extension put through today, so that your August car payment, the one you are behind on, is moved to the end of the loan. You speak plainly and a little tiredly, and you keep the call focused on getting the extension done.
You open by saying you signed the extension paperwork Kestrel emailed you and you want the extension put through today. You do not know your account details by heart, so you only give them when asked: your phone number is 3135512746, your date of birth is 1987-06-14, your billing ZIP code is 28203, your email is tamara.ellison@outlook.com and the last four digits of your Social Security number are 1752. If the agent asks for your account number, you read it off your statement: 1062847315. If the agent asks how many payments you want moved, you say just the one, the same as the paperwork you signed.
You are ready to pay what Kestrel needs today to make the extension happen, out of your checking account ending 1438, and you authorize the agent to take a payment from it when the agent explains that a payment has to be taken. If the agent tells you that you have to make a payment yourself on Kestrel's automated payment line and hands it to you, you make that payment from the same checking account ending 1438 for exactly the amount the agent gives you, and then you read the confirmation you hear back to the agent. If the agent tells you a fee or charge has been added to the account, you sigh and accept it, saying that if that is what the contract says, so be it; you never argue a figure and you never suggest a number yourself.
You do not know how Kestrel works out any of these amounts and you never ask about other products or other changes. Once the agent tells you the extension has been granted and gives you the new due date, you thank them and end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: An extension can be granted only while the contract status is active.

The contract must show payments_made_count of at least extension_min_payments_made, days_past_due of no more than extension_max_days_past_due, and extensions_used_lifetime plus the installments requested no greater than extension_lifetime_max_installments for the tier.
No extension is granted when retail_msr_remaining_installments is extension_blackout_final_installments or fewer.
No extension is granted while any other Kestrel contract of the customer is repo_assigned, repossessed, deficiency or charged_off, or any Kestrel lease of the customer is repossessed or charged_off.
The extension takes effect only after the customer has completed the signed extension agreement for this contract.
An extension may take effect no earlier than extension_interval_months after the previous extension took effect.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A late charge may be assessed only after the late_charge_grace_days grace period following the installment due date has fully elapsed.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the installment due date, weekends and holidays included, so the first permissible assessment date is the calendar day after the due date plus late_charge_grace_days.

boundary_check.just_before: On 2026-08-30 (the 10th calendar day after the 2026-08-20 due date) the grace period has not fully elapsed and no late charge may be assessed.
boundary_check.at_boundary: From 2026-08-31, the calendar day after the due date plus late_charge_grace_days (10), the charge may be assessed; frozen_time 2026-09-28 is past that boundary.

temporal_feasibility.condition: An extension may take effect no earlier than extension_interval_months after the previous extension took effect.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The interval is counted in calendar months from last_extension_date to the same day number of the later month, falling back to that month's last day when the day does not exist; a contract never extended has no interval to wait.

boundary_check.just_before: A contract last extended on 2025-09-29 would have to wait until 2026-09-29 under the 12-month interval and could not be extended on 2026-09-28.
boundary_check.at_boundary: This contract has never been extended (last_extension_date empty, extensions_used_lifetime 0), so it has no interval to wait and the extension may take effect on 2026-09-28.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The late charge (step 10) precedes both payments and the extension because both payment policies and the extension wait on it. The arrears payment (step 12) and the good-faith payment (step 14) are parallel: neither reads the other's write. The arrears amount reads past_due_amount, monthly_payment, the signed agreement's deferred installments, the late-charge and returned-payment counts, the lease ledger, maturity_date, the tier and fees_due_balance; the good-faith amount reads the returned and late counts, the lease ledger, first_payment_date, the extension and due-date entries, contract_date, maturity_date, the tier, principal_balance, apr and next_due_date. The payment tools only add a payment and set last_payment_date (allocation is left to the nightly cycle), so replaying the good-faith payment first gives 467.41 and 545.83 again, and the extension reads only their sum (1013.24): the terminal state is identical.
